title: A 2000-2012 Gutenberg-Richter fit gave no clear M7+ share error in global M5.5+ ComCat events in 2013-2025
abstract: We tested a fixed earthquake size model with 12,848 global ComCat events. We fitted a geometric distribution in 2000-2012 and tested the M7+ share among M5.5+ events in 2013-2025. The fitted b value was 1.031. The predicted share was 2.840%, and the observed share was 3.082%. The observed-minus-predicted difference was 0.241 percentage points. Its conditional 95% three-year block interval was -0.146 to 0.606 points. The primary test gave no clear calibration error or Brier score gain over the empirical training share. Some secondary thresholds had narrow departures, without adjustment for multiple tests. They do not establish a general failure or a physical cause. Revised records, mixed magnitude types, event groups and only 13 test years limit inference. This is a size test given occurrence, not a rate or hazard forecast. Code, annual statistics, simulation draws, source hashes, a figure and an independent arithmetic audit are supplied. External event records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Fixed model and later size shares. Intervals resample years in both periods. Secondary checks have no multiple-test adjustment.

citations.reason: Prior chronological size benchmark and the same shared source. The split and records overlap; this is not independent confirmation.
